text:
It is nothing of your body,

neither your skin, nor your eyes, nor your belly,

nor that secret place we both know,

grave of our death, end of our burial.

It is not your mouth—your mouth

which is just like your sex—

nor the precise meeting of your breasts,

nor your sweetest, softest back,

nor your navel where I drink.

Nor is it your thighs hard as day,

nor your ivory knees by the fire,

nor your tiny bleeding feet,

nor your scent, nor your hair.

It isn't your gaze—what is a gaze?—

sad errant light, peace without an owner,

nor the album of your ear, nor your voices,

nor the dark circles sleep leaves you.

Nor is it your viper's tongue,

an arrow of wasps in the blind air,

nor the hot dampness of your suffocation

that sustains your kiss.

It is nothing of your body,

not a blade, not a petal,

not a drop, not a grain, not a moment.


It is only this place where you were,

these stubborn arms of mine.

translation.title: It Is Nothing of Your Body
